# Kenya

> [!summary] Data available
> Dish-level coverage is strong thanks to [[World Wide Dishes]]: 85 dishes (71 Kenya-only), heavily Swahili-coast, with Luo, Borana and other cultures. Other food datasets are thin ([[WorldCuisines]] 7); there is no national FCT in the vault and no recipe corpus; plants via [[CMAUP]] (264) and compounds via the [[Global]] backbone.

## Foods & dishes
- [[World Wide Dishes]]: **85 dishes (71 Kenya-only)**; free-text ingredients, no amounts or method, plus eating context (time of day, occasion, utensils, local-language name). Kiswahili 41 dishes, Luo 6; regions Coast 28, Western 8; culture Swahili 19. Examples: potato bhajia, mukimo, omena, nyenyi, arrow roots, ashir. One of six countries with a 30-dish test set; 450 community image-review rows.
- [[WorldCuisines]]: 7 dishes (1 Kenya-only: githeri); Wikipedia-style descriptions naming ingredients, no amounts.
- No Kenyan recipes in Food.com, RecipeDB2, CulinaryDB (beyond the pan-African label) or FmLAMA; no BLEnD file.

## Ingredients & food composition
- No national FCT is in the vault or `Backlog/`. The [[FAO INFOODS global databases]] candidate (priority 2, directory of 308 tables) is where a national or regional table would be found. Fallback: [[USDA FoodData Central]] by name matching.
- Plant occurrence: [[CMAUP]] 264 plants; [[NPASS]] 11 species–compound pairs.

## Compounds & traditional medicine
- [[Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases|Duke]]: only 20 ethnobotany records (16 taxa).
- [[CMAUP]] plant → disease links for its 264 plants; [[KNApSAcK Family]] lists Kenya on its World map, but African flag pages were not scraped (counts unknown).
- Compound → effect chains come from the global backbone via [[Global]] ([[FooDB]], [[CTD]], [[Phenol-Explorer]], [[SpiceRx]], [[DDID]] for food–drug interactions).

## Gaps
- No Kenyan FCT processed and no recipes with amounts.
- The coast dominates World Wide Dishes; Kikuyu, Kalenjin and pastoralist diets are thin.
- Traditional medicine is almost absent (20 Duke records).
